prescribing.source: CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers, by Geography and Drug (national) and by Provider and Drug

days_covered.label: a proxy, not a PDC
days_covered.file_note: file-based days covered held back: the file carries 85.1% of national claims, under the 95% it needs

file.population: prescribers with 11 or more claims for the drug (the file population)
file.note: file-based days covered held back: the file carries 85.1% of national claims, under the 95% it needs

volume_deciles.note: Not computed: CMS does not say whether its national prescriber count includes prescribers with fewer than 11 claims, so the prescribers missing from the file cannot be ranked

caveats: Days covered is 30-day fills times 30 over beneficiaries times 365: a proxy, not a PDC. It falls when patients start or stop during the year as well as when they miss doses, and it can pass 1 for a drug given more often than monthly, since CMS counts every fill as at least one 30-day fill.
The provider file leaves out any prescriber with fewer than 11 claims for the drug, so its figures, the deciles among them, describe that population and not every prescriber.
prescribing.part_b_note: CMS Spending by Drug, 2024: Part B is 98% of Medicare's spend on this drug, and these Part D files do not cover it.

formulary.scope_label: Medicare Part D plans only, Sep 2026 release, contract year 2026; excludes employer, PACE and demonstration plans
formulary.source: CMS Monthly Prescription Drug Plan Formulary and Pharmacy Network Information
formulary.zero_reason: Medicare pays for it mainly under Part B, as a drug given in the clinic, so Part D plans do not list it
caveats: Excludes employer, PACE and demonstration plans. Counts formularies and plans, not people: the file carries no enrolment. Tiers are each plan's own, so only the specialty tier count compares across plans.
Fee-for-service and managed care prescriptions. Amounts are before Medicaid rebates, so this is volume, not revenue.
CMS suppresses small package rows, so a quarter that has any is a lower bound.
